source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Modes of Nutrition
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Green plants that synthesise food from CO2 and water using sunlight show
questions.explanation: Holophytic nutrition is photosynthetic autotrophy typical of green plants.

questions.stem: Plants that cannot prepare their own food and depend on other organisms are
questions.explanation: Heterotrophic plants include parasites, saprophytes and insectivores.

questions.stem: Orobanche, which lacks chlorophyll and draws food from host roots, is a
questions.explanation: Broomrape (Orobanche) is a holoparasite on roots; Rafflesia is another total root parasite.

questions.stem: Viscum (mistletoe), which is green yet taps the host stem, is a
questions.explanation: Viscum and Loranthus photosynthesise but take water and minerals from the host stem.

questions.stem: Monotropa, a flowering plant without chlorophyll, obtains food from
questions.explanation: Indian pipe (Monotropa) and bird’s-nest orchid (Neottia) are textbook saprophytes.

questions.stem: Insectivorous plants digest trapped insects chiefly to obtain
questions.explanation: They still photosynthesise; insect prey supplements nitrogen on poor soils.

questions.stem: Drosera (sundew) traps insects with
options: a snap-trap of two hinged lobes only
questions.explanation: Sundew leaves bear mucilaginous tentacles that bend over the prey.

questions.stem: In a lichen the alga supplies food while the fungus mainly provides
questions.explanation: The mycobiont shelters the phycobiont and absorbs minerals; the alga photosynthesises.

questions.stem: Root nodules of legumes harbour bacteria of the genus
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes N2 in a mutualism with legume roots.

questions.stem: The specialised sucking organs of Cuscuta that penetrate the host are
questions.explanation: Haustoria of dodder tap host xylem and phloem.

questions.stem: Santalum (sandalwood), which is green but attached to host roots, is a
questions.explanation: Sandal is a hemiparasite on roots; it photosynthesises but draws water and minerals from hosts.

questions.stem: Utricularia (bladderwort) captures prey in
questions.explanation: Bladderwort is an aquatic insectivore with suction bladders on the submerged shoots.

questions.stem: Rafflesia, famous for its huge flower, is nutritionally a
questions.explanation: Rafflesia lacks chlorophyll and vegetative shoots and lives as a holoparasite on Tetrastigma roots.

questions.stem: Which statement about holophytic nutrition is incorrect?
options: Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials
Organic food is synthesised by the plant
The plant must always feed on a living host
questions.explanation: Holophytes are autotrophs; dependence on a living host is parasitism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a heterotrophic mode in plants?
questions.explanation: Holophytic photosynthesis is autotrophy; the other three are heterotrophic habits.

questions.stem: Which plant is a total (holo-) parasite?
questions.explanation: Dodder lacks chlorophyll and is a total stem parasite; the others are hemiparasites.

questions.stem: Which statement about Loranthus is correct?
options: It is a green partial stem parasite
It is a total root parasite without chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Loranthus (like Viscum) is a leafy hemiparasite on tree branches.

questions.stem: Neottia (bird’s-nest orchid) is cited in textbooks as a
questions.explanation: Neottia lives on decaying organic matter, often via mycorrhizal fungi.

questions.stem: Insectivorous plants are still green because they
options: photosynthesise and only supplement nitrogen from prey
feed only by haustoria on trees
questions.explanation: They are mixotrophic: carbon from photosynthesis, extra N (and minerals) from insects.

questions.stem: Dionaea (Venus flytrap) captures insects by
options: rapid closure of a two-lobed leaf trap
questions.explanation: Touch-sensitive lobes snap shut; pitchers are Nepenthes and bladders are Utricularia.

questions.stem: Which statement about lichen nutrition is incorrect?
options: It is a mutualistic dual organism
The algal partner is the phycobiont
The fungal partner is the mycobiont
Both partners are always total parasites of a third plant
questions.explanation: A lichen is alga + fungus living together, not a holoparasite on a third host.

questions.stem: Which association is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation: Cuscuta is a stem parasite with haustoria, not a nodule symbiosis.

questions.stem: Haustoria of a parasitic angiosperm are meant to
options: absorb water and food from the host
store starch as a potato tuber
questions.explanation: Haustoria are absorbing outgrowths that connect parasite tissues to host vascular strands.

questions.stem: Which plant is incorrectly classified by nutritional mode?
questions.explanation: Monotropa is saprophytic, not a stem parasite.

questions.stem: The pitcher of Nepenthes functions in nutrition as a
questions.explanation: The pitcher is a modified leaf that holds digestive fluid and insect prey.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pair of plant and nutritional habit.
questions.explanation: Loranthus is a green partial stem parasite, not a saprophyte.
